paragraphs: AirBadge sells identity management software to airports in the United States, aimed at the badge office that issues and renews credentials. The company says it puts all of its resources into aviation so the software fits airport operations and TSA regulations. The product is described as built for 1542 and part 139 airports.

Applicants and badge holders enter their own details into the system. Those details are then sent directly to integrated systems, which removes a round of rekeying. It automates badge applications, appointment scheduling, training and testing, and cuts manual entry at fingerprinting, physical access control and TSC. Authorized signatories use it to invite new hires to apply and to authorize or block renewals. It runs on fully managed cloud infrastructure.

The site says more than 50 airports in the United States use it. It presents itself as a fit for airports of any size. The company announced LenelS2 factory certification and membership in the LenelS2 OpenAccess Alliance Program. Its software interfaces with the LenelS2 OnGuard access control system. Deployment is pitched in weeks rather than years.

quote.text: Built exclusively for 1542 and part 139 airports
